case_name: Union of India and Others v A. Sanyasi Rao and Others

statutes.act: Act Was Inserted By The Finance Act
Occurs In Chapter Vi Of The Act

Act And Held That The Said Provision Is Only An Adjunct To And Explains The Provisions Of Section 206C And Does Not Dispense With The Regular Assessment In Accordance With The Provisions Of The Income Tax Act
Does Not Suffer From Any Constitution
Also Does Not Suffer From Any Constitution
And Section 206C Of The Income Tax Act

facts: In this batch of cases writ petitions filed u/art. 32 of the Constitution of India and civil appeals and special leave petitions filed u/art. 136 of the Constitution of India substantially similar questions arise for consideration.
The matter arises under the Income Tax Act, 1961.
Various assesses challenged the aforesaid provisions as ultra vires and beyond legislative competence and also violative of Arts. 14 and 19(1)(g) of the Constitution of India in a few High Courts.
A few High Courts have read down the provisions of Section 44AC of the Act.
Feeling aggrieved by the same, the assesses have come up in appeal.
The Union of India has come up in appeals.
Certain other assesses have challenged the aforesaid provisions directly u/art. 32 of the Constitution of India.
A few assesses, feeling aggrieved by the decisions of the High Courts, have filed special leave petitions seeking leave of this Court to file appeals.
issues: The validity of Sections 44AC and 206C of the Income Tax Act, 1961
Whether the provisions are ultra vires and beyond legislative competence
court_reasoning: It appears that Government wanted to get over the problems in assessing income and recovering tax in the case of persons dealing in country liquor, timber, forest produce, etc.
The business of the above mentioned persons existed only for a short period -a year or two.
There was evasion on a large scale.
